limitations: The first 100 Hz held-attitude run failed, but final-version prediction-disabled forward/stop/resume repeated successfully and a separate full-motion plus 30-second-stance run also passed. The failure has not been consistently reproduced; prediction is not proven necessary or a unique fix. Initial IMU-age sequences match; asynchronous MPC policy timing differs. This is not a diagnosis of the physical robot.
The 4 ms delay and joint friction are assumed stress inputs, not measurements. They were combined; this is not an independent identification of each effect or a delay stability margin.
Motor delay is additional to one outer cycle plus physics-step phase. Friction is smooth dissipative Coulomb/viscous load, excluding stiction, backlash, efficiency and actual servo bandwidth.

Fortress prediction uses synchronized sensor acquisition stamps. Prediction remains opt-in in both paths pending stronger evidence; hardware AHRS/gyro timing is not verified. FDILink now preserves attitude host-receipt age, not device acquisition age.
The true IMU internal latency, bus buffering, per-motor sample times, torque calibration and mechanical response remain unmeasured; real sensor noise and bias were not reproduced.
Controller periods in these runs use simulation time. These tests do not certify onboard 500 Hz / 50 Hz wall-clock deadlines.
Low-speed stability passed at the tested settings; forward velocity tracking retains error. No PD, weight or hardware friction compensation tuning is claimed.
